title: Finding and mapping fields · Level 3
slo: Match OCR text values to the correct business fields.

exercises.question_text: Which techniques can be used for field mapping and association? Select all that apply.

options.rationale: Proximity analysis uses closeness, alignment, position, and reading order. It supports label-value pairing.
NER identifies entities such as dates, amounts, and names. It is a linguistic clue for field association.
Reading order follows natural text flow. It can associate labels with nearby values.
Ingestion receives text and metadata from OCR. Mapping uses clues to pair candidate values with fields.
options.better_fit: Use ingestion at the start to receive OCR results and metadata.

exercises.explanation: Correct. These techniques use spatial or linguistic clues to pair values.

exercises.question_text: A value's position can help distinguish an invoice number from a customer ID or phone number.

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: A number could be placed in the wrong field.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: Bounding boxes, page locations, and reading order help interpret a number.

exercises.explanation: Correct. Position provides context for the same-looking value.

exercises.question_text: A vendor sends the same standardized invoice form daily. The specialist sees the same labels and positions each time. Which approach best fits?

options.rationale: The layout, labels, and positions are stable. Templates fit repeated known forms.
Machine learning learns from examples across documents. A fixed form already supports simpler explicit rules.
options.better_fit: Use it when layouts vary and a corpus of examples is available.

feedback.intrinsic: The specialist could add unnecessary model-training work.
feedback.instructional: Repeated labels and positions are strong signals for templates.

options.rationale: Generative extraction uses an LLM to match text to schema fields. The stable layout makes direct template rules the closer fit.
options.better_fit: Use it when an LLM must match changing content to a schema.

feedback.intrinsic: The workflow could become more complex than needed.
feedback.instructional: Choose templates when field positions are already known.

options.rationale: Ingestion receives OCR results and metadata. It does not select a method for detecting the fields.
options.better_fit: Use it when receiving OCR text, confidence, position, and layout information.

feedback.intrinsic: The system would have inputs but no detection method.
feedback.instructional: Ingestion supplies input; templates use known labels and positions.

exercises.explanation: Correct. The repeated layout strongly favors templates.

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: The relationship between the method and its inputs would be unclear.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: Name the method, then the LLM, then its text and schema inputs.

exercises.correct_answer: Prompt-based extraction gives an LLM document text and a schema
exercises.explanation: Prompt-based extraction gives the LLM the text to inspect and the schema defining requested fields.

exercises.question_text: Proximity analysis can use closeness, alignment, and position to pair labels with values.

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: A nearby amount could be linked to the wrong label.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: Proximity analysis uses closeness, alignment, position, and reading order.

exercises.explanation: Correct. These spatial relationships support key-value pairing.

exercises.question_text: A purchase-order team receives supplier forms with varied layouts and has labeled examples. Which machine-learning training choices can help extract supplier and product fields? Select all that apply.

options.rationale: Supervised learning uses labeled field-location data. The team has labeled examples.
Multi-modal learning combines text, visual, and positional features. Those features help across varied layouts.
Self-supervised learning can learn from large document corpora. It can support document-pattern understanding.
Manual templates rely on stable layouts and explicit rules. The varied layouts and available examples support learned methods.
options.better_fit: Use manual templates for stable known forms with consistent positions.

feedback.intrinsic: The team could need many rules as layouts vary.
feedback.instructional: Labeled examples and varied forms support machine-learning training choices.

exercises.explanation: Correct. Each learning approach can support detection across varied forms.

exercises.question_text: Field extraction only lists text found by OCR and does not assign business meaning.

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: The extracted value would remain unassigned.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: OCR finds text; field extraction maps it to meaningful labeled fields.

exercises.explanation: Correct. It identifies what a value means and where it belongs.

exercises.question_text: A logistics manager processes shipping documents from many carriers and has a corpus of examples. Which reasons support machine learning-based detection? Select all that apply.

options.rationale: Machine learning learns field relationships from example documents. The manager has a relevant corpus.
Transformer-based models can use contextual cues. This helps interpret fields across carrier layouts.

options.text: It can use visual and position features
options.rationale: Multi-modal learning can use visual and positional features with text. Those features represent layout relationships.
A fixed layout favors template detection. Machine learning can learn from a varied example corpus.
options.better_fit: Use one fixed layout as a reason to select template-based detection.

feedback.intrinsic: The manager could reject a useful approach because forms vary.
feedback.instructional: Varied layouts and a corpus of examples support machine learning.

exercises.explanation: Correct. Examples, context, and multiple feature types support the decision.

exercises.question_text: A regulatory team processes one fixed government form. It needs fast, explainable extraction and can create rules for the form. Which approach should it choose?

options.rationale: The form is fixed and the team can create rules for known positions. Templates are fast and explainable in this setting.
Machine learning learns relationships from examples. The stated need for fixed-form rules and explainability favors templates.
options.better_fit: Use it for varied layouts supported by a corpus of examples.

feedback.intrinsic: The team could overlook the direct fit of transparent rules.
feedback.instructional: Fixed layout, manual rules, speed, and explainability support templates.

options.rationale: Generative extraction uses an LLM and schema. The team already has a fixed form suited to explicit rules.
options.better_fit: Use it when LLM schema matching is the required capability.

feedback.intrinsic: The solution could be less direct to audit.
feedback.instructional: For a fixed form, templates provide the explainable rule-based choice.

options.rationale: Mapping associates candidates after detection. It does not choose the initial fixed-form detection method.
options.better_fit: Use it when values must be paired through spatial or linguistic clues.

feedback.intrinsic: Candidates could be paired without a method for finding them.
feedback.instructional: The required detection approach for a known layout is template-based detection.

exercises.explanation: Correct. Fixed forms and explainability fit templates.

exercises.question_text: The step that determines that a recognized value belongs in a labeled business field is ___.

parts.text: The step that determines that a recognized value belongs in a labeled business field is

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: The value would not receive a business-field interpretation.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: Use field extraction for the step that assigns meaning to recognized OCR values.

exercises.explanation: Field extraction gives recognized text a business role, such as invoice date or total amount.

exercises.question_text: An insurance-claims team receives changing form layouts. Its analyst needs an LLM to match text to fields in a defined schema. Which approach best fits?

options.rationale: This approach uses an LLM to match text to defined schema fields. That is the decision requirement in the scenario.
Templates rely on known layouts and manual rules. Changing layouts and LLM schema matching point elsewhere.
options.better_fit: Use templates for fixed layouts with known labels and manually created rules.

feedback.intrinsic: The team could need many template changes as layouts shift.
feedback.instructional: An LLM matching text to a schema indicates generative schema extraction.

options.rationale: Machine learning learns from a corpus of examples. The key requirement here is direct LLM schema matching.
options.better_fit: Use machine learning when example documents train extraction relationships.

feedback.intrinsic: The analyst could focus on training instead of providing the needed schema.
feedback.instructional: The LLM-and-schema requirement identifies generative schema extraction.

options.rationale: Mapping pairs candidates with fields through clues. It does not name the LLM-based detection approach.
options.better_fit: Use mapping when candidates are linked by proximity or linguistic patterns.

feedback.intrinsic: The analyst could associate values without choosing the specified LLM method.
feedback.instructional: The scenario asks for generative schema extraction.

exercises.explanation: Correct. An LLM matching text to an explicit schema is generative schema extraction.

exercises.question_text: Put the pieces in the correct order.

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: Location details would be detached from the text they describe.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: Start with ingestion, then state the text and metadata it receives.

exercises.correct_answer: OCR ingestion receives raw text and positional metadata from the OCR pipeline
exercises.explanation: Ingestion receives recognized text together with metadata about location and order.
